---
title: "DoWhy tutorial series"
description: "A hands-on tutorial series for causal graphs, identification, estimation, refutation, GCM workflows, and reporting with DoWhy."
categories: [DoWhy, Python, Causal Graphs, Refutation]
---

DoWhy is the tutorial track for explicit causal assumptions: model the graph, identify the estimand, estimate the effect, and refute or stress-test the result.

<figure class="course-page-figure">
<img src="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/outputs/figures/01_core_workflow_dag.png" alt="DoWhy causal workflow DAG connecting treatment, outcome, confounders, and observed variables">
<figcaption>Figure: A DoWhy causal workflow DAG used to connect assumptions, identification, estimation, and refutation (adapted from Tutorial 01: Core Workflow, From Question To Refutation).</figcaption>
</figure>

## Tutorial Sequence

<div class="notebook-guide">
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/00_environment_and_library_tour.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/00_environment_and_library_tour.html">00: Environment And Library Tour</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Sets up the DoWhy environment, introduces the library objects, and uses a compact synthetic decision problem to show how graphs, data, and estimands enter the workflow.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/01_core_workflow_model_identify_estimate_refute.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/01_core_workflow_model_identify_estimate_refute.html">01: Core Workflow, From Question To Refutation</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Builds the central DoWhy rhythm: state the causal question, encode assumptions in a graph, identify the estimand, estimate the effect, and run refuters before making a claim.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/02_causal_graphs_dags_and_assumptions.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/02_causal_graphs_dags_and_assumptions.html">02: Causal Graphs, DAGs, And Assumptions</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Focuses on graph construction, variable roles, adjustment sets, and common DAG mistakes so the package API remains tied to explicit assumptions rather than decoration.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/03_backdoor_adjustment_and_confounding.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/03_backdoor_adjustment_and_confounding.html">03: Backdoor Adjustment And Confounding</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Shows how backdoor adjustment works in DoWhy, why confounding changes treated-control comparisons, and how adjustment choices affect an estimated treatment effect.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/04_regression_matching_and_propensity_estimators.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/04_regression_matching_and_propensity_estimators.html">04: Regression, Matching, And Propensity Estimators</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Compares several estimators for the same estimand, emphasizing what changes across regression adjustment, matching, and propensity-based workflows.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/05_weighting_overlap_and_common_support.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/05_weighting_overlap_and_common_support.html">05: Weighting, Overlap, And Common Support</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Studies inverse-probability weighting as an implementation and a diagnostic problem, with attention to overlap, weight instability, and whether the target population is credible.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/06_frontdoor_iv_and_natural_experiments.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/06_frontdoor_iv_and_natural_experiments.html">06: Frontdoor, IV, And Natural Experiments</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Extends identification beyond simple backdoor adjustment by introducing frontdoor logic, instrumental variables, and quasi-experimental designs in a DoWhy style.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/07_cate_and_heterogeneous_effects.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/07_cate_and_heterogeneous_effects.html">07: CATE And Heterogeneous Effects</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Moves from average effects to variation across units, using CATE-style thinking to support targeting, subgroup interpretation, and decision rules.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/08_refuters_placebos_negative_controls_sensitivity.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/08_refuters_placebos_negative_controls_sensitivity.html">08: Refuters, Placebos, Negative Controls, And Sensitivity</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Treats refutation as a core part of causal reporting, showing how placebo tests, negative controls, and hidden-confounding stress tests can challenge a result.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/09_graph_discovery_and_graph_refutation.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/09_graph_discovery_and_graph_refutation.html">09: Graph Discovery And Graph Refutation</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Uses candidate graph discovery as a source of hypotheses, then shows why discovered structure still needs domain review, constraints, and causal refutation.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/10_gcm_structural_causal_models.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/10_gcm_structural_causal_models.html">10: GCM Structural Causal Models</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Introduces DoWhy's graphical causal model tools for modeling mechanisms, fitting structural relationships, and checking whether the generated world resembles the observed one.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/11_interventions_and_counterfactuals_with_gcm.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/11_interventions_and_counterfactuals_with_gcm.html">11: Interventions And Counterfactuals With GCM</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Uses GCMs to reason about interventions and counterfactual changes, with emphasis on what is being changed, what is held fixed, and how outputs should be interpreted.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/12_mediation_direct_and_indirect_effects.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/12_mediation_direct_and_indirect_effects.html">12: Mediation, Direct, And Indirect Effects</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Breaks an effect into mediated and direct pathways, showing how graph choices and mediator assumptions shape the meaning of a decomposition.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/13_root_cause_anomaly_and_distribution_change.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/13_root_cause_anomaly_and_distribution_change.html">13: Root Cause, Anomaly, And Distribution Change</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Connects causal graph reasoning to anomaly attribution and distribution shift, framing root-cause analysis as a structured causal diagnostic problem.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/14_end_to_end_observational_case_study.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/14_end_to_end_observational_case_study.html">14: End-To-End Observational Case Study</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Pulls the workflow together in an observational project, moving from problem setup through graph construction, estimation, diagnostics, sensitivity, and a final summary written for practical decision-making.</p>
</article>
<article class="notebook-guide-item">
<p class="notebook-guide-title"><a href="../../notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/15_common_pitfalls_debugging_and_reporting.html" data-site-path="notebooks/tutorials/dowhy/15_common_pitfalls_debugging_and_reporting.html">15: Common Pitfalls, Debugging, And Reporting</a></p>
<p class="notebook-guide-description">Closes with practical failure modes: bad controls, weak overlap, graph misspecification, fragile estimates, and reporting patterns that make uncertainty visible.</p>
</article>
</div>
